problems.title: Fence (Codeforces 363B)
problems.description: Find the k neighbouring planks with the smallest total height among up to 150,000. Summing every block from scratch is O(n·k) and too slow; keep a running sum for O(n). Difficulty 1100.

problems.title: Interesting drink (Codeforces 706B)
problems.description: Every day, count the shops whose price fits the day's budget. Sort the prices once, then answer each day with binary search (std::upper_bound). Difficulty 1100.

problems.title: Helpful Maths (Codeforces 339A)
problems.description: Rewrite a sum like 3+2+1 so the numbers are in non-decreasing order. Practises sorting the parts of a string. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Gravity Flip (Codeforces 405A)
problems.description: Columns of cubes fall to the right when gravity switches. Notice that the result is just the column heights sorted. Difficulty 900.

problems.title: Twins (Codeforces 160A)
problems.description: Take the fewest coins so your total is strictly more than what's left. Sort in descending order and take the biggest first. Difficulty 900.

exercises.title: Weird Algorithm (CSES)
exercises.description: Follow a simple rule (even: halve it, odd: 3n+1) until n reaches 1, printing every value. An algorithm written as exact steps; the values outgrow int, so use long long.

exercises.title: Intro to Tutorial Challenges (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Find the position of a value in a sorted array. Solve it with linear search, then try binary search.

exercises.title: Binary Search (LeetCode 704)
exercises.description: Write binary search yourself on a sorted array; the solution must be O(log n). Test it with 1 and 2 elements.

exercises.title: Insertion Sort - Part 1 (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Insert the last element into the already-sorted part, printing the array after every shift. See how a simple O(n²) sort moves elements.

exercises.title: Distinct Numbers (CSES)
exercises.description: Count the distinct values among up to 200,000 numbers. Sort first, then count where neighbours differ: O(n log n).

exercises.title: Fibonacci Number (LeetCode 509)
exercises.description: Compute the n-th Fibonacci number recursively with a base case, then rewrite it with a loop and compare.

challenges.title: Algorithms: Searching
challenges.description: Measure, then search. Do the three exercises in order (an algorithm as exact steps, linear search, binary search), then the two Codeforces problems: Fence is about complexity, Interesting drink about binary search.

challenges.title: Algorithms: Sorting & Recursion
challenges.description: Start with the exercises (insertion sort, sort-then-count, recursive Fibonacci), then the Codeforces problems, roughly from easiest to hardest: Helpful Maths, Gravity Flip, Twins. In each one, sorting is the key idea.

quizzes.title: Introduction to Algorithms
quizzes.description: Five questions on complexity, searching, sorting and recursion. Answers are revealed after you submit.

questions.question: n can be up to 200,000 and the time limit is 1 second. Which approach is too slow?
answers: Two nested loops that compare every pair of elements
A single loop over the array
Sorting once, then a binary search for each element

questions.question: What must be true before you can use binary search on an array?
answers: The array has no duplicate values
The array has fewer than 1,000 elements
The array's size is a power of two

questions.question: At most how many steps does binary search need to find a value among 1,000,000 sorted numbers?
What is the time complexity of std::sort on n elements?
What does every recursive function need so that it stops?
answers: A loop around the recursive call
A base case that returns without calling itself

lessons.title: Introduction to Algorithms
lessons.description:
What an algorithm is and how to tell a fast one from a slow one: Big-O complexity and reading constraints, linear vs binary search, selection sort vs std::sort, and a first look at recursion.

Read the lesson and the links. Then try the "Algorithms: Searching" and "Algorithms: Sorting & Recursion" challenges under Practice and the "Introduction to Algorithms" quiz.
